metadata.title: PhishVN content study: page-content fusion and paraphrase-evasion data
metadata.description:
Data behind the PhishVN study of page-content fusion and paraphrase evasion. It holds a simulated Vietnamese SMS and e-mail corpus (193 phishing lures over seven scenarios and 143 benign service notifications, both classes written by one LLM, no human-written or real message, every link an inert placeholder), two sets of LLM rewrites of every lure (attack strength uncontrolled, and held to a token-Jaccard band of 0.20 to 0.30), the pilot/extension split of the rewrites, two annotators' ratings of 50 rewrites, and 1,919 crawled Vietnamese-content web pages (207 phishing, 1,712 benign) as the models read them: visible text, 21 URL features and 33 JavaScript features per page, with label, evidence tier and capture identifier. Raw HTML, scripts and screenshots are not included. The notebook notebooks/content_paraphrase/content_paraphrase_walkthrough.ipynb in https://github.com/vuthainguyen1602/phishvn recomputes every number of the paper from these files. See README.md for the file list.

Files (see README.md for the columns):

  • synthetic_sms.csv: 209 rows, simulated SMS: phishing lures over seven scenarios and benign service notifications, both written by the same LLM
  • synthetic_email.csv: 127 rows, the same for e-mail
  • paraphrase.csv: 386 rows, two LLM rewrites of each of the 193 lures, attack strength uncontrolled: variant `a` is used for training, variant `b` for attack
  • paraphrase_band.csv: 386 rows, two rewrites of each lure whose token Jaccard similarity to the source lies in [0.20, 0.30], with that similarity in `jaccard`
  • paraphrase_pilot_ids.csv: 73 rows, the source lures of the first (pilot) rewriting batch; the rest form the extension batch
  • human_eval_pairs.csv: 50 rows, the 50 (source, rewrite) pairs two annotators rated
  • human_eval_ratings.csv: 50 rows, their ratings: meaning preserved (0/1), lure still usable (0/1), and which message is more persuasive (`A` source, `B` rewrite, `ngang` equal)
  • pages.csv.xz (xz-compressed CSV): 1,919 rows, one per crawled Vietnamese-content page: visible text, 21 URL features, 33 JavaScript features, label, evidence tier and capture identifier

SHA256SUMS lists the SHA-256 of every file.

Version 1.1.0: e-mail addresses, phone numbers and other runs of nine or more digits in the page text of pages.csv.xz are replaced by [EMAIL], [PHONE] and [NUMBER] tokens, and the models of the paper read the same masked text. Version 1.0.0 shipped the page text unmasked and is superseded by this version.
